channel.title: z3itq3ist — The Gallery of Quietly Kept Things
channel.description: Personal lore gallery and permanent digital exhibition.

item.title: PL-2019-004 — The Key to Nowhere
item.description: [Pocket Archaeology] No living witness can confirm what this key unlocks. Early theories suggested a storage locker, a forgotten bicycle chain, or a childhood diary. By 2022 it shifted out of utility and into folklore—kept on the primary keyring due to the Law of Immediate Regret: the quiet belief that discarding it will summon its matching door within forty-eight hours.

item.title: PL-2022-089 — Thermal Receipt, Table 14 (2:17 AM)
item.description: [Pocket Archaeology] On paper, this records two coffees, one plate of waffle fries, and a modest tip. In personal lore, it marks the Treaty of the 24-Hour Diner—the exact evening the curator decided to leave an exhausting job and begin again. On the reverse side, a hurried blue-ink diagram outlines a five-year plan that turned out 12% accurate and 100% necessary.

item.title: PL-2018-001 — “The Good Mug”
item.description: [Domestic Relics] Faint interior rings preserve years of Earl Grey tea, instant coffee, and late-night broth. Though structurally superior mugs occupy the same shelf, this vessel holds undisputed ceremonial rank. Guests who unknowingly reach for it are gently directed toward the decoy mugs below.

item.title: PL-2023-112 — The Parking Lot River Stone
item.description: [Domestic Relics] Geologically unremarkable, this stone earned permanent gallery placement solely for its cool weight and thumb-sized hollow. Drag to rotate the 3D specimen, or click to enter the fullscreen examination room.

item.title: PL-2024-031 — The Folded Sticky Note
item.description: [Ephemera] Inscribed in pencil: “Remember to ask about the greenhouse.” The curator no longer recalls who owned the greenhouse or whether the question was ever asked. Yet it remains—a quiet monument to past curiosity.

item.title: PL-2021-077 — The Unreturned Paperback
item.description: [Phantom Room] Some of the clearest works in a personal gallery are objects no longer on the shelf. Preserved here in quiet outline until it returns, or until its underlined lines fade into memory.
